2026 SEMA Show • Ford Frostwarden, a Bronco SUV With Over 1,200 HP, the R125 and F-250 Also in Tow
New Hot Wheels Ferrari 80th Anniversary Multipack Looks Better Than I Originally Thought
14 photos
Photo: Ministry of Diecast
Oh the weather outside is awful! I haven’t seen the sun in several days now, and it looks like my village is about to be hit by a blizzard tomorrow. That means I can’t proceed with my first Hot Wheels unboxing for November, as there just isn’t enough light for some nice shots.
I also don’t want to fully rely on my Miami-themed diorama for the job, so I’ll have to find a different solution. Meanwhile, Mattel just publicly announced the Racer Series today, which means we finally have more accurate photos of the six cars.
According to the official website, the manufacturer is betting on a “Blind Purchase” strategy which means you will get a random model with each order. That’s one way to deal with both scalpers and peg-warmers in one shot.
We will have to wait a while longer until the pricing is revealed, so let’s focus on something else for the time being. The Ferrari 80th Anniversary 5-Pack didn’t come as a surprise, as we’ve already seen teasers for it since August.
In the image that was circulating online at the time, all five cars were red, though. And the F355 Berlinetta was still in a ZAMAC phase, using Real Riders wheels. Let me walk you through the whole thing.
SF90 Stradale Photo: Ministry of Diecast The SF90 Stradale is first in line, and you might remember it debuted last year in the Factory Fresh mini-series. It was one of three brand new Ferrari Mainline castings, alongside the F40 Competizione and the 365 GTB4 Competizione.
And if you think about it, it was also only one of four modern Ferraris Mattel revealed in 2025. We had two versions of the 499P plus the RC take on the SF90 Stradale Assetto Fiorano, while all the other castings were replicas of older Italian machines.
This SF90 has had seven variations so far, all while going through four different wheel designs. The original impression was that Rosso Corsa would be the manufacturer’s go-to option for the Anniversary release.
However, it now seems we’ll be able to get a Blanco Avus variation of the supercar. Depending on how old you are, it might be the least desirable collectible in the set, though.
Testarossa Photo: Ministry of Diecast There’s a good chance everyone will want a piece of the Testarossa, as this is the casting’s second variation so far. You can still get these in the real world for less than $200,000, as its value hasn’t skyrocketed like we’ve seen with cars like the F50. I know they’re on two completely different levels, and that $200,000 is still a budget most working-class citizens can’t afford.
However, you can still dream about it, which has to count for something, right? Ronald Wong designed the casting for this year’s Car Culture: Modern Classics set and I was lucky enough to find it in a grocery store of all places.
Seeing it as a Silver Series release doesn’t mean it will automatically have a Mainline variation next, as Mattel would probably even consider creating a new casting based on a different trim for that purpose alone. I’m sure something like a Testarossa Spider would start a treasure hunt, so it might be an option for either Elite 64 or the Red Line Club instead.
If you know anything about my taste in tiny cars then it shouldn’t surprise you that I’m a huge fan of the S5 wheels on this collectible. They’re not as exciting as the Real Riders Exotics, but we should also think of the price difference. As far as I can tell, the Testarossa will be the only car in this set to feature a metal base, so there’s one more reason for you to find one soon.
812 Superfast Photo: Ministry of Diecast The Ferrari 812 Superfast is the first brand-new casting in this multipack, and it’s Ronald Wong’s creation. What a surprise! It’s one of five Ferraris he has created for 2027, and there are about eight more of them that showed up in 2025 and 2026.
We already know that the model’s successor, the 12Cilindri, is getting a Super Treasure Hunt release next year. Knowing that the 812 Superfast is one its way gives me hope that Mattel should be releasing the F12 or F12 TDF sometime within the next 24 months, too.
I can already see how the three of them together could show up in an exclusive V12-themed set, maybe alongside the 599 GTO and the 575M Maranello. It’s almost unthinkable that it won’t happen, just as it’s unthinkable not to have a GTO, F40, F50, Enzo and LaFerrari mix at some point.
Anyway, I’m daydreaming here, and I confess it’s unexpected to see the 812 Superfast making its debut sporting a Grigio Silverstone finish. It’s still better than having another red car again, don’t get me wrong! And I’m glad to see the yellow stripes running down the middle for some contrast.
F355 Berlinetta Photo: Ministry of Diecast Seeing this tiny version of the F355 Berlinetta after having driven in in Gran Turismo 7 for dozens of laps recently is a funny coincidence. I’m sure there’s no connection between the two events whatsoever, even though the timing makes it seem like it.
Of course we have Mr. Wong to thank for this casting too, and I’d say it’s quite a bold decision to release it Nero Daytona. If it loses the top it could easily serve as a Fast and Furious collectible next.
This car is obviously not as popular as Rosso Corsa but I’m sure more of them came out of the factory with it than they did in Azzuro Dino or Verde Mugello. There’s a good chance the team in El Segundo already knows what the next variation will look like, and we’ll just have to wait and see how it turns out.
Call me crazy if you will, bu I’d say this is the most desirable car in the set, as I already have a Testarossa and don’t really care about the other three ones as much.
365 GTB4 Competizione Photo: Ministry of Diecast Don’t get me wrong, the 365 GTB4 Competizione looks great in Blu Dino! It’s hand down the best variation so far if only for that reason, and we’ve had five of them by now. I unboxed the First Edition release a while ago, and have mostly ignored it since.
Switching from the 5-Spoke rims to the Retro Slot Wheels wasn’t an improvement, whereas the Star 5-Spoke, Silver Series design is a step in the right direction. I realize not every Hot Wheels Ferrari casting can become a premium model but you have to ask the question: is this 365 GTB4 Competizione “doomed” to be stuck in the entry-level categories forever?
There’s still some potential in Pop Culture with a Miami Vice replica, even it means “downgrading” to a regular Daytona. I have a feeling this multipack won’t become a peg-warmer like the basic 5-pack that you can still see in toy stores all over right now.
Even though pre-orders with some dealers started back in August, I hope there will be plenty of them to go around in a few weeks time. I got word of the launch from my buddy Zali from Ministry of Diecast, who pointed out that you can already buy the set from Rakuten in Japan. Will you be going after it, too?
